html:
On 9 April 1940 Germany invaded Norway by sea and air. After two months of fighting, with British and French help, Norway's forces gave up in June.

Germany wanted the iron ore shipped from Narvik and bases on the Atlantic. In the Oslofjord the fortress at Oscarsborg sank the cruiser Blücher, which gave the king and government time to escape. King Haakon VII refused to accept the government of the Norwegian Nazi Vidkun Quisling, whose name became a word for traitor.

The king and government went to London, and Norway's large merchant fleet served the Allies. At home a resistance grew, including the heavy water sabotage. Norway was freed in May 1945, at the end of the Second World War, and gave up neutrality to join NATO in 1949.
sum: On 9 April 1940 Germany invaded Norway by sea and air. After two months of fighting, with British and French help, Norway's forces gave up in June.
